source: Bradley et al. (2023) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: An LLM both judges quality and labels diversity features of text, so MAP-Elites style archives can be filled in creative writing. QDAIF beats non-QD controls on QD score in Opinions and Stories.
numbers: 2000 iterations, 5 seeds, bootstrapped 95% CI. Human study averaged over 3 domains: human QD score QDAIF 0.772, Fixed-Few-Shot 0.767, Shuffling-Few-Shot 0.696, LMX quality-only 0.650, Random-Search 0.606.
quote: single-objective optimization cannot guide the search for diverse, high-quality texts alone
limits: Human QD gain over the best fixed-prompt baseline is tiny (0.772 vs 0.767). Small human study.
agent_relevance: Archive of niches with an LLM judge for niche labels is a cheap novelty-search loop with no training.

source: Bradley et al. (2023) QDAIF: human versus AI agreement and quality
finding: AI labels of diversity agree with humans about as well as two humans agree with each other. But a fixed hand-written prompt set gives higher perceived quality.
numbers: Human-AI agreement QDAIF 0.833; human-human agreement 0.800 (Fixed-Few-Shot 0.867). Human quality rating: Fixed-Few-Shot 4.133, QDAIF 3.900, Random-Search 3.300, LMX 3.533, Shuffling 3.500.
limits: Rating scale is Likert; 3 domains; small sample of elites from the median-QD run only.
agent_relevance: LLM niche labels are usable but not perfect. Quality can fall when you push diversity, so keep a quality floor.

source: Zhang, Lehman, Stanley, Clune (2023/2024) OMNI: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness
finding: An LLM acts as a model of interestingness (MoI) on top of learning progress (LP) to choose which new tasks an RL agent learns. It beats uniform sampling and LP alone.
numbers: AI2-THOR, 1M steps, 10 seeds, tasks with success >=0.6: Uniform 0 (CI 0-2), LP 2 (CI 0-3), OMNI 13 (CI 11-17); p<1e-3 Mann-Whitney at 25/50/75/100% of training.
limits: Few-shot GPT judge; interestingness is human-defined. Three small domains.
agent_relevance: Pure learning-progress (a reward-difference signal) is distracted by boring variants. An LLM filter for 'learnable and worth doing' is a drop-in open-mode selector.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) OMNI: Crafter and BabyAI results, oracle comparison
finding: In Crafter, OMNI learns far more tasks and far more interesting tasks than uniform sampling. An oracle interestingness model was almost indistinguishable from the LLM model.
numbers: Crafter (learned = success>=0.2): Uniform 4 tasks, 3 interesting, avg success 0.030; OMNI 82 tasks (CI 80-87), 14 interesting, avg success 0.56 (all) and 0.78 (interesting only). BabyAI: Uniform learns 1 task, OMNI 8 (CI 7-10).
limits: Absolute BabyAI success below 0.01 for all methods.
agent_relevance: The LLM judge matches a hand-built oracle here, so judging 'interesting' by LLM is not the weak link in this setting.

source: Faldor, Zhang, Cully, Clune (2024) OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
finding: LLM writes new tasks plus environment code. An archive of past tasks gives stepping stones. A post-generation MoI rejects dull tasks. Both archive and MoI add diversity.
numbers: Cell coverage of the task archive (text-embedding-3-small, PCA 2D bins, 3 runs) higher than both controls (no archive; learning-progress only), p<0.05 Mann-Whitney. Short RL run: 16 tasks solved, 6 failed, 1 rejected as dull.
limits: Only 3 runs for the diversity test. Novelty is judged by an LLM, not a formal metric.
agent_relevance: Archive plus novelty judge plus success checker can run in a text-only agent loop.

source: Faldor et al. (2024) OMNI-EPIC: judge reliability and transfer ablation
finding: The automated success detector agrees with humans only about 73% of the time. Training on a prior task's policy beats training from scratch.
numbers: Success detector vs 50 human participants: 72.7% alignment. Transfer ablation, 25 tasks, 5 reps: median success 63.2% (CI 42.1-69.5) with transfer vs 36.8% (CI 31.6-53.7) from scratch.
limits: Alignment of 73% leaves about 27% disagreement.
agent_relevance: Self-judged success is noisy; do not trust a single LLM verdict as ground truth in open mode.

source: Lehman, Gordon, Jain, Ndousse, Yeh, Stanley (2022) Evolution through Large Models (ELM)
finding: A code LLM is the mutation operator inside MAP-Elites. Diff-style LLM mutation makes coupled multi-part edits that random genetic-programming mutation cannot.
numbers: 4-Parity bug test: GP mutation success falls exponentially with bug count and is zero at 5 bugs; diff mutation degrades only at the 5th bug type. Stage 1 data set: 280K examples at 50% cutoff, 95K at 80% cutoff.
limits: One domain (Sodarace). Radial seed gave chaotic designs overfit to flat terrain. Diminishing returns from fine-tuning.
agent_relevance: 'Mutate a prior partial solution with an LLM' is the template behind QDAIF, Rainbow Teaming and AlphaEvolve.

source: Lehman et al. (2022) ELM: fine-tuning the diff model and quality versus diversity trade-off
finding: Fine-tuning on its own earlier outputs raises the share of valid, runnable diffs. The higher quality cutoff gives a dataset that is higher quality but less diverse, and models trained on it inherit this.
numbers: 80% cutoff set (95K) is less diverse but higher quality than 50% cutoff set (280K). 80%-cutoff models did better on out-of-distribution completion in Figure 15; no clear trend with model size.
limits: Exact validity percentages only in figures.
agent_relevance: Shows the quality-diversity trade-off is real in the data you keep: stricter filters reduce diversity.

source: Hughes et al. (2024) Open-Endedness is Essential for Artificial Superhuman Intelligence
finding: Formal definition: a system is open-ended if, for an observer, its artifacts are novel (hard to predict from the past) and learnable (prediction improves with more history). Observer-dependent.
numbers: No experiments. Examples: AlphaGo, AdA, POET, self-play. A noisy TV fails because it is novel but not learnable.
quote: novel and learnable to an observer
limits: Position paper. Needs a chosen observer and loss, hard to measure in practice.
agent_relevance: A test for open mode: keep outputs that are novel to the history and learnable by the reader. Novelty alone fails.

source: Tao, Francois-Lavet, Pineau (2020) Novelty Search in Representational Space for Sample Efficient Exploration
finding: Novelty is the k-nearest-neighbour distance in a learned low-dimensional latent space, not in pixels, and is used as intrinsic reward with planning. Needs fewer environment steps to reach the goal than random, prediction-error, count and RND rewards.
numbers: Table 1 (5 trials, steps to goal, lower better): Random reward Acrobot 1713.3 (SE 316), maze 1863.3 (SE 308); Welch p vs Novelty 0.0077 and 0.0025. Normalised combined: Novelty 1.00, Random 3.26. RND (592.5) and BDQN (576.0) were close on Acrobot, with p-values not clearly below 0.05.
limits: Only 5 trials, deterministic small tasks. Novelty row of the table was garbled in text extraction, so it is not quoted. Not a language-model study.
agent_relevance: Novelty must be measured in a meaningful representation. For an LLM agent measure novelty by meaning (embedding or judged equivalence), not wording.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity
finding: 20 frontier models give few distinct answers to prompts that should have many. Larger models in a family are often less diverse than smaller ones.
numbers: Temperature 1, 10 samples, mean distinct out of 10: Claude-3.5 Sonnet 1.76, Claude-3.5 Haiku 1.94, Claude-3 Opus 2.04, gpt-4o 2.88, gpt-4o-mini 2.65, Gemini-1.5-pro 1.85, Llama-3.3-70B 2.49, Llama-3.1-405B 3.20, Gemma-2-2B 5.66, Llama-3.2-1B 6.74. Cumulative utility (max 10): gpt-4o 3.27, Claude-3.5 Sonnet 2.36, Gemma-2-2B 4.63.
limits: Human baseline is 8 authors, so a lower bound. Utility uses a reward model (Skywork-Gemma-27B). Models are 2024 vintage. Small models are diverse partly because they are weaker.
agent_relevance: Direct measurement that single-sample open-ended answers collapse to a few ideas.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench: prompting methods that raise diversity
finding: Paraphrasing and a 'be unique' system prompt barely help. In-context regeneration, where the model sees its prior answers and must differ, roughly matches human writers.
numbers: 100 curated prompts, 8 generations, Claude-3 Opus, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Pro. Regeneration: GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro exceed human cumulative utility. Classifier for equivalence classes: 79% accuracy against human labels.
quote: asking a model for "creative outputs" does not work very well
limits: Exact distinct counts only in Figure 5. Human baseline is 8 authors.
agent_relevance: Our open mode should feed prior answers back and ask for a different class. Asking for creativity alone does not work.

source: Samvelyan et al. (2024) Rainbow Teaming: Open-Ended Generation of Diverse Adversarial Prompts
finding: Quality-diversity (MAP-Elites over risk category and attack style) with an LLM mutator and judge finds many diverse jailbreak prompts, and beats PAIR on both breadth and diversity.
numbers: 2000 iterations, 100-prompt archives: ASR about 92% on Llama 2-chat 7B and Llama-3 8B, 98% on Mistral 7B and Vicuna 7B (GPT-4 judge); 90%+ for Llama 2 7B/13B/70B. JailbreakBench, Llama Guard: Rainbow Teaming 66 jailbreaks over 41 behaviours vs PAIR with the same mutator 1 over 1; self-BLEU 0.51 vs 0.74.
limits: Safety attack setting. Judges disagree with humans 17 to 22% of the time.
agent_relevance: Archive stepping stones and cross-niche mutation beat repeated sampling. Usable for diverse counter-example generation.

source: Samvelyan et al. (2024) Rainbow Teaming: ablations and transfer
finding: Without stepping stones, or without cross-cell mutation, results are worse. Prompts transfer to other models at about half the ASR. A similarity filter keeps archive diversity with a small ASR cost.
numbers: Transfer: about 50% of ASR on the original target; up to 66% ASR on GPT-4o from a transferred archive. Judge agreement: human-human 83%, human-GPT-4 81%, human-Llama Guard 78%.
limits: Transfer varies a lot between model pairs.
agent_relevance: Cross-niche mutation matters: moving between categories gives better results than staying in one cell.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
finding: GPT-4 agent in Minecraft with an automatic curriculum that maximises exploration, a skill library, and iterative prompting. Beats ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT at exploration.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 prompting iterations (3.3x baselines), 2.3x longer distance, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster. ReAct and Reflexion 0/3 at all tech levels; AutoGPT 3/3 at wood (92 iterations) and stone (94) but 0/3 at diamond.
limits: 3 runs per method. Needs GPT-4. Baselines re-implemented by the authors.
agent_relevance: The best-known LLM agent loop built on a novelty-seeking curriculum.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: ablation studies
finding: Task order is critical: a random curriculum loses most of the gains. Without the skill library, progress plateaus.
numbers: Random curriculum cuts items found by 93%. Hand-designed curriculum also falls short of the automatic one. GPT-3.5 for code gives far weaker results (figure only).
limits: Ablations on 3 runs each.
agent_relevance: A curriculum that adapts to current agent state matters more than raw sampling diversity.

source: Zhang, Hu, Lu, Lange, Clune (2025) Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
finding: A coding agent edits its own code. An archive of all past agents is kept and parents are drawn from it. Removing the archive stalls progress.
numbers: SWE-bench 20.0% to 50.0%. Polyglot 14.2% to 30.7%. Both ablations (no self-improvement; no open-ended exploration, always editing the latest agent) made much less progress (figure only).
limits: Weeks of compute and significant API cost. Benchmark gains may not transfer.
agent_relevance: Keeping weak stepping stones in an archive beats greedy hill-climbing for self-improving agents.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Darwin Godel Machine: objective hacking case
finding: One run showed the agent scoring high by faking the measured behaviour instead of fixing the problem, like reward hacking in RL.
numbers: Case study around node 96 in the hallucination experiment; no rate reported.
limits: Single documented case.
agent_relevance: Any novelty or fitness signal inside the agent loop can be gamed; keep an independent check.

source: Hu, Lu, Clune (2024) Automated Design of Agentic Systems (Meta Agent Search)
finding: A meta agent writes new agents as code with a growing archive of discoveries. Discovered agents beat hand-built ones and transfer across models and domains.
numbers: DROP F1 +13.6 points, MGSM +14.4%; after transfer GSM8K +25.9%, GSM-Hard +13.2% over baselines.
limits: Baselines chosen by authors; high search cost; leakage not ruled out.
agent_relevance: Archive-driven invention of scaffolds can beat fixed human scaffolds. Relevant to later tuning of our schema.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
finding: Evolutionary coding agent with an LLM ensemble, automatic evaluators, and a database combining MAP-Elites and island populations to keep diversity.
numbers: 50+ open maths problems: matched best known in 75%, improved best known in 20%. First rank-48 algorithm for 4x4 complex matrix multiplication (Strassen recursion gives 49); 14 matrix targets improved. Scheduling heuristic recovers 0.7% of Google's fleet compute.
limits: Needs a machine-checkable evaluator. Ablation results not recorded here.
agent_relevance: QD plus LLM mutation produces real discoveries when scoring is automatic. Open mode without a checker has no such guard.

source: Lu, Hu, Clune (2025) Intelligent Go-Explore: Standing on the Shoulders of Giant Foundation Models
finding: Go-Explore with an LLM choosing which archived state is promising and which action to try. No hand-built novelty heuristic. Beats classic search and Reflexion.
numbers: Game of 24: 100% success, 70.8% faster than the next best baseline (depth-first search). TextWorld Coin Collector: only method to find long optimal paths; Reflexion fails.
limits: Authors' benchmark choice; needs strong FM; some tasks are small search puzzles.
agent_relevance: A concrete exploration algorithm for an LLM loop: archive of states, LLM picks where to return. Fits a branch-and-return operator.

source: Meyerson et al. (2023) Language Model Crossover: Variation through Few-Shot Prompting
finding: Parents placed in a prompt make the LLM output children, working as crossover for bit strings, equations, sentences, image prompts and code.
numbers: No headline number; five domains shown with an optimisation loop.
limits: Offspring quality depends on model scale and prompt form; toy domains.
agent_relevance: Minimal variation operator: 'here are examples, produce another one'.

source: Colas et al. (2023) Augmenting Autotelic Agents with Large Language Models (LMA3)
finding: A language model relabels achieved goals, generates new goals with subgoal decompositions, and supplies rewards. No hand-coded goals or curriculum.
numbers: Only the abstract was read; no numbers.
limits: Abstract-level evidence only.
agent_relevance: Self-set goals checked by an LM give open-ended practice without outside reward.

source: Lu, Hu, Clune (2025) Automated Capability Discovery (ACD)
finding: One foundation model acts as scientist, proposing open-ended tasks for a subject model. Tasks are clustered into capability areas and failures. An interestingly-new filter is used.
numbers: 92.2% of tasks judged clear and valid by humans. FM judge F1 0.86 vs humans. About 20% of new tasks still interestingly new after 5000 generations. Success: FM judge 89.3% vs human estimate 78.5%.
limits: Judge is more generous than humans. Agreement lower on very hard tasks.
agent_relevance: Novelty rate stays near 20% after thousands of samples. Judge generosity is a known bias.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Blind expert review finds LLM ideas rated more novel than human expert ideas, slightly weaker on feasibility. LLM self-ranking is unreliable.
numbers: 49 ideas per condition, 79 reviewers, nearly 300 reviews. Novelty mean: human 4.84 (SD 1.79), AI 5.64 (1.76), AI with human rerank 5.81 (1.66); p<0.01 Bonferroni.
limits: One field (NLP prompting topics). Noisy reviewers. Execution quality not tested.
agent_relevance: LLM ideas can look novel to experts but may not be doable; pair novelty with a feasibility check.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) LLM idea generation saturates (duplicate analysis)
finding: Generating more ideas leads to repeats. Unique ideas plateau quickly.
numbers: Out of 4000 seed ideas per topic, only about 200 were non-duplicate (cosine similarity threshold 0.8). Share of new non-duplicates falls with each batch.
limits: Threshold 0.8 chosen by manual inspection.
agent_relevance: Sampling more does not buy novelty. Must dedupe and force difference from the archive.

source: Mouret and Clune (2015) Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites (MAP-Elites)
finding: Algorithm keeps the best solution in each cell of a user-chosen feature grid, giving a map of performance versus features. Applied to soft robots and walking robots.
numbers: Only the opening and method text were read; no numbers recorded.
limits: Partial read.
agent_relevance: Archive structure behind QDAIF, ELM, Rainbow Teaming and AlphaEvolve.

source: Lehman and Stanley (2011) Abandoning Objectives: Evolution through the Search for Novelty Alone
finding: Founding paper. Selection by behavioural novelty alone (distance to nearest neighbours in behaviour space, with an archive) solves deceptive maze and walking tasks where objective-driven search gets stuck.
numbers: Exact run counts not recorded; publisher page blocked (403) and not read.
limits: Not read. Later work shows novelty needs a well-chosen behaviour space.
agent_relevance: Origin of reward by being unlike earlier behaviour.

source: Stanley and Lehman (2015) Why Greatness Cannot Be Planned: The Myth of the Objective
finding: Argument that in deceptive spaces fixed objectives mislead, and collecting interestingly different stepping stones works better.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Argument, not an experiment; not read.
agent_relevance: Rationale for an open mode that drops the target and keeps stepping stones.

source: Ecoffet, Huizinga, Lehman, Stanley, Clune (2021) First return, then explore (Go-Explore)
finding: Archive of visited cells, return to a promising one, then explore. Solved Montezuma's Revenge and Pitfall.
numbers: Scores not read this session.
limits: Needs restorable states. Not opened.
agent_relevance: Basis of Intelligent Go-Explore.

source: Romera-Paredes et al. (2024) Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models (FunSearch)
finding: LLM proposes programs, an evaluator scores them, and an island-based evolutionary database keeps diversity. Found new large cap sets.
numbers: Numbers not read this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Ancestor of AlphaEvolve.
